ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AD$ is the median of $\triangle ABC$. It is known that the perimeter of $\triangle ABD$ is $25\,\text{cm}$, and $AB$ is $7\,\text{cm}$ longer than $AC$. What is the perimeter of $\triangle ACD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AD$ is the median of $\triangle ABC$,\\
it follows that $BD=CD$,\\
therefore, the difference in the perimeters of $\triangle ABD$ and $\triangle ACD$ is $(AB+BD+AD)-(AC+CD+AD)=AB-AC$.\\
Since the perimeter of $\triangle ABD$ is $25\,cm$ and $AB$ is $7\,cm$ longer than $AC$,\\
the perimeter of $\triangle ACD$ is: $25-7=\boxed{18}\,(cm)$.

It is known that P(ABD)=25 cm, therefore P(ACD)=25-7=18 cm. Final answer: 18 cm.
